person.name: Lane Faison
person.headline: Engineering student at Trinity College who works on aerospace and defense strategy and builds AI tools by directing coding agents.

education.program: Engineering major, minor in Formal Organizations

personal: Spent a semester in Rome and speaks functional Italian.
Plays tennis; former president of Club Tennis at Trinity.
background: Former president of Club Tennis and of the ASME student chapter at Trinity; serves on the executive board of the Entrepreneurship Club.

experience.org_description: A boutique aerospace and defense strategy and M&A advisory firm in the Washington, D.C. area.
experience.summary: Buy-side commercial due diligence and market and revenue modeling on three aerospace and defense acquisitions. Client and deal names are confidential. On one model, cut a contract win-rate assumption after finding that a new-entrant competitor had bid, and defended the change to the partner. Also built two internal AI tools (see project rsa-ai-tools).

When a forging supplier slowdown delayed turbine blades for an engine-maker customer by several weeks, presented the evidence to the customer, explained the supplier renegotiation, and told them up front that the fix would add further delay. Helped roll out standard operating procedures that cut costs.

projects.name: Reusable LN2-cooled reentry heat shield (senior engineering capstone, ENGR 483)
projects.summary: Four-person team project to design a lighter or more reusable heat shield than the ablative AVCOAT standard for capsule reentry. The team compared a transpiration-cooled porous lattice against a conical shield cooled by liquid nitrogen flowing through radial pipes, chose the radial-pipe cone, and built a serpentine cooling-channel rig with a thermocouple grid to validate the pipe-flow and conduction models. Lane led the problem framing, the design alternatives and down-select, the final-design justification, and the conclusions.

annotation.what: A senior design project: a liquid-nitrogen-cooled conical heat shield concept for capsule reentry, plus a test rig that validates its thermal models.
annotation.why: Capsules have no reusable heat shield; ablatives are single-use. Active LN2 cooling was chosen over transpiration cooling after a trade study.

projects.name: Firm-knowledge retriever and house-style slide skill (Renaissance Strategic Advisors)
projects.summary: Built solo with Claude Code during the RSA internship: (1) a retriever that indexes past engagement material, extracts keywords and summaries, and is queried by an agent at the start of a new engagement to surface relevant prior projects; (2) a slide-building skill trained on sanitized prior firm decks so new slides follow the firm's visual structure.

projects.name: Defense market-research toolkit (Claude skills)
projects.summary: A set of Claude skills for defense market research: navigating and extracting line items from DoD budget justification books (J-books); a research workflow that answers program, contract, and budget questions in DACIS; and a company market-profile framework that classifies how a defense company participates in a market across five archetypes, using its role on named programs, its contract tier, and its partnerships, checked against FPDS-NG, SAM.gov, and USAspending.

projects.name: PowerPoint automation skills
projects.summary: Skills that refresh the numbers behind native PowerPoint charts from a new data table (including the embedded workbooks, growth-rate callouts, and axes) and that align and distribute logos on slides.

projects.name: Interview-preparation tools
projects.summary: A fully editable behavioral-interview flashcard web app for consulting interviews, with interviewer follow-ups two layers deep, deployed on Netlify; and a case-interview practice grader that transcribes a recorded practice case, measures pace, filler words, hedges, and pauses, grades it against a seven-dimension rubric with quoted evidence, and keeps a running ledger across sessions.

projects.name: AI Integration coursework (CPSC 415, Fall 2026)
projects.summary: Weekly labs built with a coding agent and documented through intent, spec, and decision logs: a single-page memorization trainer (week 1); a command-line chat client that reports model and token use (week 2); a support-message classifier with structured JSON output and a five-case eval comparing two models (week 3).
